title: 自己実験としての名乗り —— 非流派が独我流を名乗るとき、何が欠けるか
description:
稽古は、裏切りと騙し討ちと不意打ちの三つを排除することで成り立っている。相手の意思と情報と時間を、こちらに与えた状態が稽古である。与えなければ稽古にならず、与えれば技が実際に効くかを決める条件ではなくなる。

一人で行う稽古は、この排除をもう一段進める。ゆえに独我流は、その三つに構造的に弱い。そこから帰結が一つ出る。独我流が最後に依拠するのは技術ではなく、三つが作動する局面を発生させない能力である。本稿はこれを戦略的能力と呼び、独我流の究極形態と位置づける。

この帰結は強さからではなく弱さから導かれたものであり、現段階では測定ではなく主張である。本稿は公開ノートであり、査読を受けていない。

Training in a martial art is constituted by the exclusion of three things: betrayal, deception, and ambush. A training session is a state in which the partner's intent, information, and timing have all been handed to the practitioner. Withhold them and there is no training; grant them and the conditions that decide whether a technique actually works are no longer present.

Solitary training pushes this exclusion one step further. It follows that a solitary practice is structurally weak against precisely those three. What such a practice finally relies on is not technique. It is the capacity to prevent the situations in which the three operate from arising at all. This paper calls that capacity strategic capability and locates it as the terminal form of a solitary practice.

The conclusion is derived from weakness, not from strength. At the present stage it is a claim, not a measurement. This is a public note and has not been peer-reviewed. The English text follows the English preprint in preprint/.
notes: The text was written with a language model, Claude (Anthropic), at the author's request. The author decided the argument and wrote the account of experience, and is responsible for it. Claude is not an author. Not peer-reviewed. The text is CC BY 4.0.
